1. **P1 — Catalog filters can replace the host policy.**  
   [input.ex:116](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/input.ex:116) accepts every atom key. [input.ex:71](/Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_integration/jido_connect/apps/jido_connect/lib/jido_connect/catalog/input.ex:71) then merges filters after host runtime options.

   An action input with `filters: %{policy: nil}` removes a supplied deny policy. I reproduced this option replacement. `Catalog.call_tool/3` passes these options to Connect, where an absent policy permits operations with `host_policy_required?: false`. Existing catalog tests cover invalid filter shapes, but not runtime keys inside filters.

   **Smallest correction:** Permit only declared filter keys for both atom and string input. Reject runtime keys before the merge.

Acceptance: Reproduce the reported case against current source, apply the smallest correction described above, and add focused verification of both the failing case and supported behavior. For documentation/design work, update the public contract and verify its examples/callers. Preserve tenant, scope, lease, and host ownership boundaries. Use fresh matching v3 dependencies for final verification; saved local v2 build artifacts do not establish v3 conformance.

Do not modify jido_mcp or publish packages. Full source review and its coverage/verification limits are preserved in the parent epic comments.
title: Catalog filters can replace the host policy
